title: HeavyTailedHessianVector.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization on R^d, permitting nonconvex objectives. The gradient is L-Lipschitz, the Hessian is ρ-Lipschitz in operator norm, and a global lower bound m satisfies f(x0)−m≤Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query (x, none) returns an unbiased stochastic gradient g(x,ξ), with a fresh independent sample. No function values or sample reuse are supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedHessianVector.lean: spec.Query and spec.admissible oracle answer and gradient unbiasedness; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A query (x, some v) returns an unbiased stochastic Hessian-vector product H(x,ξ)v. Each gradient or Hessian-vector response counts as one call against the same fixed budget. Full Hessian access is not supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedHessianVector.lean: spec.Query and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and Convergence

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For public p∈(1,2], E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖^p≤σg^p and E‖(H(x,ξ)−∇²f(x))v‖^p≤σh^p‖v‖^p for every x,v. The Hessian noise bound is directional, not an operator-norm moment bound. Variances may be infinite when p<2. Sample matrices need not be symmetric or derivatives of a common random loss.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedHessianVector.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible moment bounds and declaration of H

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean space R^d with positive finite dimension d and its Euclidean norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Oracle seeds are IID across calls. All parameters are public: d, Ω, L, ρ, σg, σh, p, Δ, ε and x0; L,ρ,ε>0 and σg,σh,Δ≥0. The objective, estimators and sampling law are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedHessianVector.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy ‖∇f(x)‖≤ε.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The output is measurable and satisfies both stationarity conditions jointly with probability at least 2/3 over algorithm and oracle randomness, within a fixed oracle budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: At the same returned point, ⟨v,∇²f(x)v⟩≥−√(ρε)‖v‖² for every v, equivalently λmin(∇²f(x))≥−√(ρε).

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The second-order stationarity target is standard, but the oracle permits infinite-variance noise with only directional p-moment control of Hessian-vector errors, without sample symmetry, common-loss structure or sample reuse.

descriptionHtml:
Heavy-Tailed Second-Order Stationarity

We consider minimizing a twice differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥1. Its gradient and Hessian are Lipschitz with constants L>0 and ρ>0, respectively, and a given point x0 has objective gap at most Δ≥0 above a global lower bound. The oracle returns unbiased gradient or Hessian-vector estimates using independent samples, with bounded error moments of order p∈(1,2], allowing heavy-tailed noise. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ satisfying both ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε and ⟨v,∇2f(x¯)v⟩≥−ρε∥v∥2 for every v∈Rd, with probability at least 2/3. Here the norm and inner product are Euclidean.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). We use ∥⋅∥op for the induced operator norm on linear maps from Rd to itself. The algorithm receives d, the measurable sample space Ω, L, ρ, the noise bounds σg,σh≥0, p, Δ, ε, and x0∈Rd.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Gradient and Hessian regularity). The function f is differentiable everywhere, its gradient is differentiable everywhere, and, for every x,y∈Rd, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Lower bound and initial gap). There exists m∈R such that f(x)≥mfor every x∈Rd,f(x0)−m≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Unbiased oracles with bounded moments). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and jointly measurable maps g:Rd×Ω→Rd,H:Rd×Ω→L(Rd,Rd), where L(Rd,Rd) is the space of linear operators equipped with its operator norm. For every x,v∈Rd, the random vectors g(x,ξ) and H(x,ξ)v, with ξ∼ν, are Bochner integrable and satisfy Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[H(x,ξ)v]=∇2f(x)v. Their error moments are integrable and obey Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥p]≤σgp,Eξ∼ν[∥H(x,ξ)v−∇2f(x)v∥p]≤σhp∥v∥p. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν. They are independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

At call k, the algorithm may query any x∈Rd for the vector g(x,ξk), or any pair x,v∈Rd for the vector H(x,ξk)v. Each call returns one of these two vectors and uses the next sample in the same sequence. Both query types count toward a single total oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯∈Rd must be measurable and satisfy P(∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε,⟨v,∇2f(x¯)v⟩≥−ρε∥v∥2for every v∈Rd)≥23, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.ContinuousLinearMap

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedHessianVector

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  σg : ℝ
  σh : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Space (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)

def secondOrderAccurate (p : Params) (f : Space p → ℝ) (x : Space p) : Prop :=
  ‖gradient f x‖ ≤ p.ε ∧
    ∀ v : Space p, -Real.sqrt (p.ρ * p.ε) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ⟪v, fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v⟫

abbrev spec : OracleTemplate.Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Space p → ℝ
  Query p := Space p × Option (Space p)
  Reply p := Space p
  Output p := Space p
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.d ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σg ∧ 0 ≤ p.σh ∧
    1 < p.p ∧ p.p ≤ 2 ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ∃ (g : Space p → p.Ω → Space p)
      (H : Space p → p.Ω → Space p →L[ℝ] Space p)
      (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → p.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → p.Ω) => ξ k) (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => p.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x, v) seed =>
            match v with
            | none => g x seed
            | some w => H x seed w } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    Differentiable ℝ (gradient f) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ p.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ m : ℝ, (∀ x, m ≤ f x) ∧ f p.x0 - m ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry H) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ p.p) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ p.p ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ p.σg ^ p.p) ∧
    (∀ x v, Integrable (fun ω => H x ω v) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x v, ∫ ω, H x ω v ∂(P0 : Measure _) = fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v) ∧
    (∀ x v, Integrable (fun ω => ‖H x ω v - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v‖ ^ p.p)
      (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x v, ∫ ω, ‖H x ω v - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v‖ ^ p.p ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤
      p.σh ^ p.p * ‖v‖ ^ p.p)
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      (P : Measure _).real {ω | secondOrderAccurate p f (output ω)} ≥ 2 / 3

end LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedHessianVector
